Updated assessment incorporating SLOOS:
- Credit supply is easing broadly: banks reported easing standards across CRE (multifamily and nonfarm nonresidential), residential mortgage categories (including jumbo, QM/non-QM, and HELOCs), and consumer credit (credit cards, autos), alongside actions like higher card credit limits and lower auto loan rates. Foreign banks also eased CRE standards and saw stronger CRE demand.
- Demand signals are improving on balance: banks expect stronger demand for C&I and credit cards; consumer loan demand was stronger. Some categories showed softer current demand (e.g., C&I and autos at certain banks) and standards were unchanged for government mortgages, but the forward tilt is constructive.
- Implications for the Nov 3, 2021 FOMC message: easier bank lending standards and firmer expected demand support the Committee’s view of continued economic gains with policy still accommodative during taper. However, the Financial Stability Report’s vulnerabilities (elevated valuations, compressed risk premiums, nonbank fragilities) and mixed spots in loan demand argue for only a modest upgrade in tone.

Net: slightly more positive than the prior read, but still cautious given stability risks and supply/inflation uncertainty.
